citations.narrative:
One dog and one rabbit were not handled as carefully as possible by research facility staff as specified below.
On June 8, 2026, beagle # 1710330 was inadvertently sedated with Dexmedetomidine and Butorphanol for a study to
which it was not assigned. The technicians involved reported that the morning was busy and they felt rushed. The
technicians did not follow the required animal identification procedures outlined in the animal use protocol, including
carrying the cage card with the animal, verifying ear tattoos, shaving the ear to confirm the tattoo, and reviewing prior
body weights when a discrepancy was flagged. Upon discovery of the error, sedation was reversed and the dog
recovered uneventfully.
On June 24, 2026, rabbit 2M009 died during a surgical procedure following multiple unsuccessful intubation attempts and
subsequent airway management challenges. The technician reported that they observed blood during the third intubation
attempt, after which they placed a supraglottic device (v gel). The animal exhibited signs of compromised oxygenation,
including a darkened tongue, leading to the decision to transition from the v gel to mask anesthesia. The rabbit
experienced respiratory arrest, and the technician initiated manual ventilation, but the animal ultimately arrested and died.
Necropsy revealed laryngeal fold perforation, abdominal distension, diffuse gastrointestinal gas, and regurgitation fluid in
the trachea and bronchi. Cause of death was determined to be airway loss. Staff interviewed about the intubations
reported feeling pressured to proceed rapidly to maintain the study schedule.
The rabbit and dog were not handled as carefully as possible by facility staff resulting in the death of one rabbit during
anesthesia and the unnecessary sedation of one dog. The handling of all animals should be done as expeditiously and
carefully as possible in a manner that does not cause trauma, physical harm, behavioral stress, or unnecessary
discomfort. Both incidents were identified by the research facility, and appropriate corrective measures were implemented
prior to this inspection.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the IACUC chair and the attending veterinarian.
